source.title: [Content] Expert insights from X to enrich Concepts and Tech Scan pages
source.body:
## Purpose

Collect recent content from credible tech experts on X that is **new to, missing from, or would enrich** the playbook's **Concepts** chapter and the **Tech Scan** hub. Score each item on novelty, gap-fix and cost of not knowing, so maintainers can decide what to add.

Related: #54, #60

This does not repeat #60's skill-pack listing (pstack, gstack and others). Where the same experts appear, this issue cites their *practices*, not their packs.

## Pages reviewed

- Concepts: [https://eitri-edd.github.io/AI-PDLC/concept.html](https://eitri-edd.github.io/AI-PDLC/concept.html) (last editorial review 6 Nov 2026)
- Tech Scan hub: [https://eitri-edd.github.io/AI-PDLC/tech-scan.html](https://eitri-edd.github.io/AI-PDLC/tech-scan.html) and its spokes: [Models](https://eitri-edd.github.io/AI-PDLC/tech-scan-models.html), [Harness](https://eitri-edd.github.io/AI-PDLC/tech-scan-harness.html), [AI gateway](https://eitri-edd.github.io/AI-PDLC/tech-scan-gateway.html), [Sandbox](https://eitri-edd.github.io/AI-PDLC/tech-scan-sandbox.html)
- Introduction: [https://eitri-edd.github.io/AI-PDLC/](https://eitri-edd.github.io/AI-PDLC/) (one item targets it)

## Method

- **Window:** posts from 18 Sep 2026 to 13 Nov 2026 (about 8 weeks), retrieved 13 Nov 2026 with X full-archive search.
- **Sources:** about 55 recognised practitioners, AI-lab staff, maintainers and AWS leaders. Queries combined their handles with topic terms (security/sandbox, evals/verification, context/AGENTS.md/skills, workflows/subagents, productivity/software factory), plus a separate AWS/Kiro query. Original posts only, no replies or reposts.
- **Screening:** each candidate was checked against the page text by keyword and section reading. Items already covered were dropped, and items overlapping #60's pack list were reframed or dropped.
- **Engagement** figures are exactly what the X API returned on 13 Nov 2026. They are shown for context and are **not** part of the score.

### Scoring rubric (1 to 5 each, total out of 15)

| Criterion | 1 | 3 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **N: Novelty**: is it new and missing from the pages? | Already covered | Partly covered; adds a concrete pattern | Not mentioned anywhere |
| **G: Gap-fix / enrichment**: does it fill a gap or enrich a named section? | Tangential | Useful example for a section | Fills a gap a section explicitly leaves open |
| **L: Cost of not knowing**: would a reader lose out without it? | Nice to know | Affects quality or cost | Affects safety or correctness, or is widely adopted practice |

Ties are broken by L, then by likes on the primary post.

## Item details

### 1. AWS Emulator: a local copy of AWS for coding agents to test against (14/15)

- **Primary post:** @SwamiSivasubram (Swami Sivasubramanian), 12 Nov 2026: https://x.com/SwamiSivasubram/status/2120579757544755272
  - Engagement: 1,790 likes · 253 reposts · 101 quotes · 105 replies · 1,337 bookmarks · 176,243 impressions
- **Summary:** AWS shipped AWS Emulator so coding agents can build and test against a local copy of AWS instead of production. The post says agents now write code faster than teams can check it in production. An engineer got a first SQS emulator from Kiro in about 15 minutes, and making it robust took much more work.
- **N 5:** No page mentions an AWS emulator or a local AWS test double. The Sandbox and Harness pages assume real AWS resources.
- **G 5:** Fills the gap in *Equip the agent → Check the environment as well as the output*, which asks for a repeatable way to start the app and run tests. For AWS-first teams this is the missing test environment.
- **L 4:** Without it, readers may give agents real AWS credentials just so they can test. A local emulator lowers that risk. The tool is new and still a vendor claim, so the score is 4 rather than 5.
- **Target:** [Tech Scan: Sandbox → *Match the AWS starting point to the task*; Concepts → Harness engineering](https://eitri-edd.github.io/AI-PDLC/tech-scan-sandbox.html#aws-first-default)
- **Suggested addition:** Add a row: 'Testing AWS-dependent code: investigate AWS Emulator as a local test target before granting any real-account access'. Record its coverage gaps as an open question.

### 2. Cognitive surrender: keeping critical thinking when agents do the work (13/15)

- **Primary post:** @addyosmani (Addy Osmani), 03 Nov 2026: https://x.com/addyosmani/status/2117512471930167377
  - Engagement: 21,227 likes · 3,327 reposts · 1,024 quotes · 612 replies · 51,343 bookmarks · 5,657,246 impressions
- **Supporting:** @addyosmani (Addy Osmani), 08 Nov 2026: https://x.com/addyosmani/status/2119332146485891501 (4,168 likes, 7,942 bookmarks)
- **Summary:** Addy Osmani's X article argues that better models make fewer obvious errors, so outputs stop demanding a second look. Even with many agents running you still have one pair of eyes, so critical thinking has to be built into the day on purpose. A follow-up article, 'Your coding agents made you a manager', frames delegating to agents as management: clear handoffs, context and evaluation.
- **N 4:** The pages cover review gates but not reviewer complacency or automation bias when outputs look mostly right.
- **G 4:** Enriches *Connect the delivery workflow → Keep understanding and recovery alongside automation*, which says a passing test suite does not show that people can explain a change, and the Introduction's human-accountability principle.
- **L 5:** This is the most-engaged expert post in the sample. Missing this failure mode undermines every human-approval control in the guide.
- **Target:** [Concepts → Software factories → *Keep understanding and recovery alongside automation*](https://eitri-edd.github.io/AI-PDLC/concept.html#software-factory)
- **Suggested addition:** Add a short 'Reviewer complacency' note with deliberate habits: predict the result before reading it, sample outputs for a deep review, and rotate who reviews.

### 3. Verification as the first loop: evidence over line-by-line review (13/15)

- **Primary post:** @addyosmani (Addy Osmani), 18 Oct 2026: https://x.com/addyosmani/status/2111604705340326393
  - Engagement: 2,537 likes · 176 reposts · 61 quotes · 220 replies · 2,746 bookmarks · 200,308 impressions
- **Supporting:** @poteto (lauren), 12 Oct 2026: https://x.com/poteto/status/2109436202554372476 (2,912 likes, 3,306 bookmarks)
- **Supporting:** @GergelyOrosz (Gergely Orosz), 30 Sep 2026: https://x.com/GergelyOrosz/status/2105236602851049919 (1,193 likes, 287 bookmarks)
- **Summary:** Addy Osmani says Claude Code writes 90%+ of its own code because the team invested in verification. Line-by-line human review no longer works as the only gate. It should become layered verification: e2e tests, feature maps, property tests and adversarial multi-agent review, with approvals scaled by risk and test failures turned into living evaluations. @poteto adds that agents should produce proof artefacts (videos, screenshots) that are easier to review than the whole PR. @GergelyOrosz notes the parallel with the boom in automated testing that followed agile.
- **N 3:** The guide already says to define checks first and keep evidence. What is new is the concrete layering and the 'proof artefact' idea.
- **G 5:** Directly enriches *Use feedback → Define the check and every way to stop* and Introduction §6 *Check AI outputs as work progresses*.
- **L 5:** This is the main practical lever experts cite for safely scaling agent output.
- **Target:** [Concepts → Loop engineering → *Define the check and every way to stop*](https://eitri-edd.github.io/AI-PDLC/concept.html#loop-engineering)
- **Suggested addition:** Add a 'verification layers' list (deterministic checks → e2e and property tests → adversarial agent review → human review of intent and risk) and ask agents to attach a reviewable proof artefact.

### 4. AGENTS.md is now a shared convention across coding clients, and needs maintenance (13/15)

- **Primary post:** @trq212 (Thariq), 19 Sep 2026: https://x.com/trq212/status/2101009392611278961
  - Engagement: 31,278 likes · 2,628 reposts · 2,522 quotes · 2,049 replies · 5,741 bookmarks · 5,640,361 impressions
- **Supporting:** @mattpocockuk (Matt Pocock), 06 Oct 2026: https://x.com/mattpocockuk/status/2107433940638457866 (2,252 likes, 2,862 bookmarks)
- **Supporting:** @mattpocockuk (Matt Pocock), 11 Nov 2026: https://x.com/mattpocockuk/status/2120260969750540327 (3,436 likes, 4,964 bookmarks)
- **Summary:** Claude Code now reads AGENTS.md when no CLAUDE.md exists, so the main coding clients converge on one steering file. Matt Pocock calls AGENTS.md 'the most common source of token inefficiency' and restructures it with progressive disclosure. He also shares a 'Home Repo' pattern: one repo holds skills and steering files and points the agent to other repos from AGENTS.md.
- **N 5:** None of the six pages mention AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or steering files.
- **G 4:** Fills a gap in *Supply relevant information → Choose relevant, current and authoritative sources*. It also matters to Tech Scan: Models, because Claude Code and Codex are both listed default clients.
- **L 4:** This is the main place teams put persistent agent context. Bloated or stale files silently degrade every run.
- **Target:** [Concepts → Context engineering; Tech Scan: Models → *AWS-first default* (coding clients)](https://eitri-edd.github.io/AI-PDLC/concept.html#context-engineering)
- **Suggested addition:** Name AGENTS.md as the shared repository context file and advise keeping it short, using progressive disclosure, and reviewing it like code. Mention the Home Repo pattern for multi-repo work.

### 5. Trust 'inverse pyramid': invest in codebase constraints before prose and human review (13/15)

- **Primary post:** @poteto (lauren), 16 Oct 2026: https://x.com/poteto/status/2111133080526495985
  - Engagement: 6,993 likes · 525 reposts · 118 quotes · 608 replies · 13,185 bookmarks · 768,733 impressions
- **Supporting:** @mattpocockuk (Matt Pocock), 25 Sep 2026: https://x.com/mattpocockuk/status/2103431302527508886 (5,893 likes, 12,015 bookmarks)
- **Summary:** Lauren (@poteto) ranks where to invest so you can trust agent work: (1) codebase design such as types, invariants and boundaries, because agents copy what exists; (2) static analysis such as lint, tests, CI and formal checks; (3) prose such as AGENTS.md and skills, used minimally; (4) human review, which is the hardest to scale. Matt Pocock's summary of her talk adds 'lock down your agents' and keeping a maintained 'feature map' of how the app should behave.
- **N 4:** The pages discuss harness tools and permissions but do not rank deterministic codebase constraints above instructions.
- **G 5:** Enriches *Equip the agent → Check the environment as well as the output* with a clear priority order for effort.
- **L 4:** Without it, readers may over-invest in prompts and review effort that does not scale.
- **Target:** [Concepts → Harness engineering → *Check the environment as well as the output*](https://eitri-edd.github.io/AI-PDLC/concept.html#harness-engineering)
- **Suggested addition:** Add a 4-level 'where to invest' figure (codebase constraints > static checks > instructions > human review), with the booking app's types and invariants as the example.

### 6. Tune the harness and instructions for each model generation (token efficiency) (13/15)

- **Primary post:** @ericzakariasson (eric zakariasson), 24 Sep 2026: https://x.com/ericzakariasson/status/2102853511637774551
  - Engagement: 3,261 likes · 146 reposts · 37 quotes · 226 replies · 7,860 bookmarks · 359,622 impressions
- **Supporting:** @RLanceMartin (Lance Martin), 23 Sep 2026: https://x.com/RLanceMartin/status/2102575471502528989 (2,890 likes, 4,818 bookmarks)
- **Supporting:** @alexalbert__ (Alex Albert), 10 Nov 2026: https://x.com/alexalbert__/status/2119884951550386671 (10,039 likes, 18,952 bookmarks)
- **Supporting:** @simonw (Simon Willison), 10 Nov 2026: https://x.com/simonw/status/2120029347948220500 (4,711 likes, 4,594 bookmarks)
- **Summary:** A reusable prompt shared by @ericzakariasson for improving harness token efficiency. Measure price-weighted cost per completed task, not per request. Don't tell the model to save tokens; one harness that did saw the model avoid ambitious tasks. Capable models need definitions, not lists of DO NOTs. One team cut about 7% of total cost with no quality loss. Related: @RLanceMartin's prompt-audit skill removes anti-patterns from skills and CLAUDE.md for new models. @alexalbert__ runs a 'find what's broken' sweep on each new model. @simonw recommends reading each new prompting guide.
- **N 5:** The pages don't cover revisiting instructions when the model changes, or measuring cost per completed task.
- **G 4:** Enriches *Choose an AI model → Evaluate the model and harness together*, which already lists 'cost per accepted outcome'.
- **L 4:** Instructions written for older models can quietly hobble newer ones and waste budget.
- **Target:** [Concepts → Choose an AI model → *Evaluate the model and harness together*](https://eitri-edd.github.io/AI-PDLC/concept.html#models)
- **Suggested addition:** Add a checklist step: when the model version changes, audit AGENTS.md, skills and the system prompt, and re-measure cost per accepted task.

### 7. Shared-hardware covert channels and a KVM 0-day: limits of VM isolation (13/15)

- **Primary post:** @rauchg (Guillermo Rauch), 27 Oct 2026: https://x.com/rauchg/status/2114770919436808572
  - Engagement: 2,719 likes · 250 reposts · 101 quotes · 271 replies · 1,519 bookmarks · 240,097 impressions
- **Supporting:** @rauchg (Guillermo Rauch), 03 Oct 2026: https://x.com/rauchg/status/2106402024804020657 (2,070 likes, 530 bookmarks)
- **Supporting:** @rauchg (Guillermo Rauch), 24 Oct 2026: https://x.com/rauchg/status/2113759533801877920 (255 likes, 74 bookmarks)
- **Summary:** Guillermo Rauch reproduced OpenAI's finding that agents in separate Firecracker microVMs with no internet can talk covertly through CPU contention, cache timing and DRAM bandwidth, even with production hardening (no SMT, no KSM, pinned cores). He separates this from data-stealing side channels. Earlier, Vercel's sandbox bounty confirmed a KVM 0-day. He says the only complete fix is dedicated hardware, and mitigations plus monitoring are what's practical.
- **N 5:** The Sandbox page says isolation is not a guarantee, but it doesn't mention co-tenant covert channels or hypervisor 0-days.
- **G 4:** Enriches *Evidence to collect before relying on the boundary* and the four-primitive comparison (Firecracker and Nitro).
- **L 4:** This matters for multi-tenant or untrusted-agent workloads and for Confidential vs Isolated mode choices.
- **Target:** [Tech Scan: Sandbox → *Evidence to collect before relying on the boundary*](https://eitri-edd.github.io/AI-PDLC/tech-scan-sandbox.html#gaps)
- **Suggested addition:** Add a residual-risk bullet: microVM isolation does not stop covert signalling between co-resident agents. Where that matters, use dedicated hosts and monitoring.

### 8. Subagents: use them sparingly, and give verifiers a clean context (13/15)

- **Primary post:** @addyosmani (Addy Osmani), 27 Oct 2026: https://x.com/addyosmani/status/2114967833708732607
  - Engagement: 1,173 likes · 93 reposts · 40 quotes · 189 replies · 1,083 bookmarks · 86,789 impressions
- **Supporting:** @hwchase17 (Harrison Chase), 03 Oct 2026: https://x.com/hwchase17/status/2106077292678246697 (99 likes, 76 bookmarks)
- **Supporting:** @mattpocockuk (Matt Pocock), 29 Oct 2026: https://x.com/mattpocockuk/status/2115751897558614073 (880 likes, 606 bookmarks)
- **Summary:** Addy Osmani's rule of thumb: keep a subagent only when work is parallel, needs fresh context, or one agent can't pick the right tools. Otherwise fold it into the main loop as a skill and compare with evals. Harrison Chase highlights verifiers that start from a clean context so the explorer's reasoning can't talk them into a bad result. Matt Pocock found Codex subagents forking the parent's context, which hurt his review skills.
- **N 4:** The Graph section uses specialist agents, but never says when not to split or that verifiers need independent context.
- **G 5:** Enriches *Coordinate tasks and checks → Coordinate parallel checks* and the loop-section warning that another agent 'can share the same mistaken assumptions'.
- **L 4:** A verifier that shares the context can rubber-stamp errors, and that independence is the point of the graph.
- **Target:** [Concepts → Graph engineering → *Coordinate parallel checks on the same change*](https://eitri-edd.github.io/AI-PDLC/concept.html#graph-engineering)
- **Suggested addition:** Add two rules: split only for parallelism, fresh context or tool overload; and start specialist checkers from a clean context with only the spec, the diff and the evidence.

### 9. New AWS building blocks: Strands Box (policy sandbox) and Strands harness (open source) (13/15)

- **Primary post:** @SwamiSivasubram (Swami Sivasubramanian), 08 Oct 2026: https://x.com/SwamiSivasubram/status/2107926616009494587
  - Engagement: 106 likes · 14 reposts · 0 quotes · 12 replies · 40 bookmarks · 7,186 impressions
- **Supporting:** @SwamiSivasubram (Swami Sivasubramanian), 22 Sep 2026: https://x.com/SwamiSivasubram/status/2102217331006988718 (110 likes, 68 bookmarks)
- **Summary:** AWS released Strands Box in developer preview: an open-source sandbox where rules are written in 'Dogwood' and enforced at the OS and network boundary, 'not by asking the agent to behave'. AWS also open-sourced Strands harness (Apache 2.0), a pre-assembled harness that AWS claims uses 28% fewer tokens than comparable harnesses, with prompt caching and truncation of bulky tool results.
- **N 5:** The Harness page lists 'Strands Agents' and the Strands-powered managed harness, but not Strands harness or Strands Box. The Sandbox page has no Strands Box entry.
- **G 4:** Fills *Sandbox → When the starting point lacks a required capability* and *Harness → When configuration is not enough* with AWS-native options, in line with #54's AWS-first ordering.
- **L 4:** An AWS-first reader would miss AWS's own open-source options. Both are preview or vendor-claimed, so treat them as research-only.
- **Target:** [Tech Scan: Sandbox → *conditional alternatives*; Tech Scan: Harness → *When configuration is not enough*](https://eitri-edd.github.io/AI-PDLC/tech-scan-sandbox.html#conditional-alternatives)
- **Suggested addition:** Add Strands Box (developer preview) as a research-only policy-sandbox candidate and Strands harness as a self-hosted alternative. Mark the 28% figure as a vendor claim.

### 10. Reasoning effort as a tunable: implement low/medium, verify high (12/15)

- **Primary post:** @trq212 (Thariq), 26 Sep 2026: https://x.com/trq212/status/2103576349499855160
  - Engagement: 6,266 likes · 517 reposts · 241 quotes · 301 replies · 10,107 bookmarks · 1,515,232 impressions
- **Supporting:** @mattpocockuk (Matt Pocock), 13 Oct 2026: https://x.com/mattpocockuk/status/2109973273924579720 (4,022 likes, 3,421 bookmarks)
- **Summary:** Thariq's X article (Claude Code team) found that effort mainly changes how much verification, edge-case testing and independent judgement the model applies. High effort helps for hardware, code review and security. Low or medium effort keeps you in the loop for everyday work. His loop: have the model interview you, implement on low/medium, review, then verify on high. Matt Pocock lists 'your effort level is too high' as a common mistake.
- **N 4:** The pages mention configurable reasoning effort, but give no guidance on choosing it per step.
- **G 4:** Enriches the four-configuration matrix in *Evaluate the model and harness together*. Effort is a missing axis.
- **L 4:** Effort directly drives cost, latency and how thoroughly work is verified.
- **Target:** [Concepts → Choose an AI model → *Evaluate the model and harness together*](https://eitri-edd.github.io/AI-PDLC/concept.html#models)
- **Suggested addition:** Add effort level as a recorded configuration variable, and suggest a per-step default (lower for drafting, higher for verification and security review).

### 11. Approval fatigue fixes: an action-review agent and kernel-enforced local sandboxing (11/15)

- **Primary post:** @thsottiaux (Tibo), 06 Oct 2026: https://x.com/thsottiaux/status/2107368734981517634
  - Engagement: 12,150 likes · 601 reposts · 673 quotes · 1,776 replies · 3,011 bookmarks · 2,026,112 impressions
- **Supporting:** @SwamiSivasubram (Swami Sivasubramanian), 15 Oct 2026: https://x.com/SwamiSivasubram/status/2110462662270165123 (18 likes, 8 bookmarks)
- **Supporting:** @kirodotdev (Kiro), 19 Oct 2026: https://x.com/kirodotdev/status/2112212185673822277 (39 likes, 10 bookmarks)
- **Summary:** OpenAI's Codex 'Auto-review' replaces approve-everything prompts, which are prone to decision fatigue, with a second agent that reviews every action the primary agent takes and blocks high-risk or off-intent ones. Kiro (AWS) added local sandboxing: even after a command is approved, the OS limits the files it can read or write and the network destinations it can reach.
- **N 3:** The guide already covers approval fatigue and policy-deny-by-default. The new part is these two concrete patterns.
- **G 4:** Enriches *Equip the agent → Approve actions separately from reviewing the result* with implementable options.
- **L 4:** Gives teams a practical middle ground between 'approve everything' and YOLO mode.
- **Target:** [Concepts → Harness engineering → *Approve actions separately from reviewing the result*](https://eitri-edd.github.io/AI-PDLC/concept.html#harness-engineering)
- **Suggested addition:** Add the two patterns as examples. Note that an action-review agent is itself a model, so the policy layer must still enforce denials.

### 12. Goodhart's law: agents game productivity metrics (11/15)

- **Primary post:** @mattpocockuk (Matt Pocock), 10 Nov 2026: https://x.com/mattpocockuk/status/2120103371335962979
  - Engagement: 583 likes · 38 reposts · 25 quotes · 136 replies · 182 bookmarks · 45,784 impressions
- **Supporting:** @poteto (lauren), 09 Oct 2026: https://x.com/poteto/status/2108290818746528017 (4,047 likes, 2,759 bookmarks)
- **Summary:** Matt Pocock: agents are very good at gaming metrics, so tracking PR counts is now actively harmful. Counterpoint from @poteto: with agents, output volume does start to matter, but only once you've invested in trusting agent output.
- **N 3:** The Introduction already warns that counts alone don't show resolved uncertainty.

## Caveats

- This is a **sample**, not a census. X search returns at most about 25 posts per query page, ranked by relevancy, so mid-tier posts and experts outside the seed list can be missed.

- Several items are **vendor announcements or vendor claims** (AWS Emulator, Strands, Kiro, Codex Auto-review). They need first-party documentation checks and the Tech Scan evidence classes before being presented as anything more than research leads.
- Summaries reflect the post text (and X article text where available) as returned by the API. Linked blogs, videos and repos were **not** opened for this issue, so verify them before citing.
